results.title: Cytokine context shapes antigen-presenting and matrix-producing states of cancer-associated fibroblasts.
results.authorString: Song F, Chen Q, Huang D, Zhang Y, Han D, Rao W, Li M, Gao Y, Zhang R, Zhu H, Wang S, Jiang X, Lin S, Bi D, Zhang H, Wei Q, Qin H.
results.abstractText: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit remarkable functional heterogeneity, with conserved subtypes observed across diverse malignancies. However, their shared roles in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) and their dynamic plasticity remain incompletely understood. In this study, through integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling across four cancer types, we identified two distinct immunomodulatory CAF states, termed antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) and matrix-producing CAFs (mCAFs). Across multiple solid tumors, apCAFs were associated with enhanced anti-tumor immune features and favorable prognosis, whereas mCAFs were associated with immunosuppressive characteristics and poorer clinical outcomes. Spatial analyses revealed distinct localization patterns of apCAFs and mCAFs within the TME. Functionally, patient-derived apCAFs promoted T-cell migration, proliferation, and activation, whereas mCAFs suppressed these responses in vitro. Pan-cancer analyses further revealed a strong inverse correlation between apCAF and mCAF abundance across tumor tissues. Mechanistically, IFN-γ and TGF-β-associated signaling contexts were linked to distinct CAF transcriptional programs, with IFN-γ promoting apCAF-associated features and TGF-β favoring mCAF-associated features, suggesting a potential role of cytokine context in shaping CAF state heterogeneity. Clinically, apCAFs correlated with favorable immunotherapy response, whereas mCAFs predicted poor therapeutic outcomes. Collectively, these findings identify conserved immunomodulatory CAF subtypes across cancers, reveal distinct cytokine-associated CAF programs, and support stromal reprogramming as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

results.title: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Molecular Continuity in Pathogenesis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Normal Epithelium to Precancerous Lesions and Carcinoma.
results.authorString: Lan L, Wang X, Jiang X, Lin X, Lai Y, Tan W, Zhang S, Lin D, Wu C.
results.abstractText: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) develop from the stratified epithelia of the esophagus, head and neck, lung, and skin, providing a tractable model to investigate how altered epithelial fields progress toward invasive cancer. Across SCC subtypes, evolution often begins before overt malignancy, with age- and exposure-associated mutant clones expanding within histologically normal epithelia. As lesions advance, early driver selection becomes coupled to copy number alterations, chromosomal instability, and epigenetic remodeling, whereas later stages are shaped by branching diversification, cellular plasticity, and regionally constrained selection. Despite tissue-specific differences, several recurrent principles emerge, including clonal expansion within mutated normal fields, transition bottlenecks marked by genome-scale instability, and the spatial organization of subclonal architecture and invasive-front states. In this review, we synthesize recent progress in the temporal ordering and spatial patterning of SCC evolution and discuss how genetic alterations, epigenetic remodeling, and tissue ecology jointly drive disease progression. We further highlight the implications for early interception, biomarker development, immune evasion, and evolution-informed prevention and therapy.

results.title: Epitope-diverse autoantibodies induce neutrophil-epithelial niches driving kidney injury in ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis.
results.authorString: Nishide M, Matsushita H, Mizuno Y, Nishimura K, Lelliott PM, Kawada S, Fujii T, Kamikawaji S, Nonaka T, Motooka D, Metsugi S, Shimagami H, Miyamoto AT, Kato Y, Tsujimoto K, Edahiro R, Shirai Y, Yamamoto Y, Naito Y, Konaka H, Izumi M, Naito M, Nakanishi Y, Namba-Hamano T, Inoue K, Takahashi A, Mizui M, Nakazawa S, Kakuta Y, Funakoshi K, Terada M, Irie M, Torizawa T, Omiya R, Smith NI, Isaka Y, Nonomura N, Okada Y, Hattori K, Narazaki M, Kumanogoh A.
results.abstractText: Autoantibody-mediated inflammation drives tissue injury in autoimmune diseases, yet how pathogenic antibodies evoke local immune activation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that spatially organized neutrophil-epithelial niches contribute to kidney injury in myeloperoxidase (MPO)-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated glomerulonephritis. Single-cell-resolved spatial transcriptomics of treatment-naïve patient kidney biopsies identified early-phase inflammatory niches enriched with HAVCR1+ injured proximal tubular epithelial cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and TREM2+ macrophages. Injured epithelial cells expressed chemokines including CXCL6 and CXCL16, defining a microenvironment associated with local immune cell accumulation. Neutrophils within these niches were characterized by transcriptional programs enriched for type II interferon and Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-related signaling. Mechanistically, combinations of monoclonal anti-MPO antibodies recognizing distinct epitopes enhanced neutrophil activation and induced pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis in mice, recapitulating key aspects of epithelial injury observed in human kidneys. One-armed anti-MPO antibodies engineered to minimize FcγR engagement ameliorated kidney injury in mice. Together, these findings identify pathogenic neutrophil-epithelial niche formation as a driver of autoimmune kidney injury.

results.title: Oncogenic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to clinical practice.
results.authorString: Li C, Yin X, Zhou S, Wen J, Yu J, Meng X.
results.abstractText: Targeted therapy has revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients harboring oncogenic alterations, and next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) significantly increase blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, leading to improved disease control and survival benefits. However, several issues remain to be addressed, including the selection of more appropriate and individualized agents, the emergence of TKI resistance, and the challenging management of central nervous system (CNS) progression. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the efficacy and safety of TKIs and targeted specific antibodies in advanced or metastatic patients with common or rare mutations, providing guidance in selecting the optimal agent. We further explore the mechanisms underlying drug resistance and regimens aimed at overcoming resistance. In nonmetastatic resectable or unresectable NSCLC, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeted agents and current issues requiring further research. In addition, we distinguish current and potential therapeutic strategies for patients with baseline brain metastasis (BM) and those without baseline BM who subsequently develop brain progression, leading to more effective and personalized treatment. Finally, we provide perspectives on challenges and future directions in the identification and treatment of oncogenic alterations, particularly in the context of co-mutations and the heterogeneous nature of metastases, and emphasize the clinical importance of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted genetic testing and biomarker development.

results.title: IL-1β/IL-6 inflammatory crosstalk drives DNA methylation and histone remodeling associated with cytokine induced senescence in luminal breast cancer.
results.authorString: Dey Pereira S, Padam KSR, Shruptha P, Atreya A, Joshi MB, Satyamoorthy K.
results.abstractText:
Background

Chronic inflammation exerts paradoxical effects in breast cancer, inducing growth arrest while sustaining tumor progression. However, how autocrine and paracrine inflammatory cytokine induced senescence integrates with tumor-promoting behaviour remains unclear. Here, we identify a reciprocal IL-1β/IL-6 circuit that links inflammatory cues, epigenetic remodeling and cytokine induced senescence in luminal breast cancer cells.

Methods

Following treatment with IL-1β and IL-6, MCF-7 cells were examined using cell-cycle, apoptosis, reactive oxygen species flow cytometry assays, and senescence assays; RNA sequencing; global DNA methylation quantification; methylation-specific PCR; ChIP-qPCR for histone marks; cytokine ELISA; and western blotting for DNMTs and STAT3/AKT/NF-κB signaling proteins. The kinetics of IL-1β and IL-6 signaling were examined using receptor antagonism and pharmacological inhibition.

Results

IL-1β induced senescence characterized by G0/G1 arrest, elevated SA-β-gal activity, ROS accumulation and absence of apoptosis. Transcriptomic profiling revealed cell-cycle regulator repression, enrichment of senescence-associated signatures and a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype. Mechanistically, IL-1β induced increased DNMT1 and DNMT3A expression, elevated global DNA methylation, induced promoter-specific DNA methylation (IL-15, HMGB2) and histone mark remodeling (IL-6, IL1RN, BCL2,BAX) at inflammatory, senescence, and apoptotic loci. IL-1 receptor antagonism attenuated these effects. IL-6 induced downstream of IL-1β, in turn activated STAT3, increased DNMT1 and DNMT3B expression, amplified IL-1β expression and tumor-promoting phenotypes, while sustaining the IL-1β induced senescence state. IL-6R blockade disrupted this axis and reduced tumor-promoting effects.

Conclusion

An IL-1β/IL-6 inflammatory loop drives epigenetic remodeling associated with cytokine induced senescence while promoting tumor-supportive signaling. IL-1β initiates the senescence program, whereas IL-6 reinforces and sustains this state through STAT3/DNMT signaling, highlighting inflammatory cytokine signaling pathways as potential therapeutic targets for breast cancer therapy.

results.title: Ferroptosis in cancer: molecular mechanisms, tumour microenvironment, therapeutic resistance, and clinical translation.
results.authorString: Dewasi G, Jain S.
results.abstractText: Ferroptosis is a distinct form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and oxidative membrane damage, and it differs fundamentally from apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis in its molecular mechanisms and execution pathways. Increasing evidence indicates that ferroptosis plays a pivotal role in cancer biology by regulating tumour initiation, progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and interactions within the tumour microenvironment (TME). Dysregulation of iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, amino acid metabolism, and antioxidant defence systems, including the System Xc⁻-GSH-GPX4, FSP1-CoQ₁₀, GCH1-BH4, and DHODH pathways, collectively determines cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis. Recent studies have further highlighted the contribution of organelle crosstalk, immune cell regulation, and stromal interactions in shaping ferroptotic responses and tumour evolution. In this review, we comprehensively summarise the molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis, its regulatory signalling networks, and the major milestones that have advanced the field. We further discuss the multifaceted role of ferroptosis across diverse malignancies, its influence on epithelial-mesenchymal transition, tumour invasion, metastasis, and immune modulation, and its emerging significance in overcoming resistance to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. In addition, we critically evaluate recent progress in ferroptosis-based therapeutic strategies, including nanomedicine, combination therapies, and translational advances, while highlighting current clinical challenges such as tumour heterogeneity, limited pharmacodynamic biomarkers, and safety concerns. Collectively, ferroptosis represents a promising therapeutic vulnerability that bridges fundamental cancer biology with precision oncology. Continued development of biomarker-guided patient stratification, targeted drug delivery systems, and rational combination strategies is expected to accelerate the clinical translation of ferroptosis-based therapies and improve outcomes for patients with refractory and treatment-resistant cancers.
